To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a series of A3AR agonistic N6-(benzyl) adenosine analogues with 2-aryylethynyl substituent were designed and synthesized, (ii) the analogues were screened in vivo (peroral administration) in mouse chronic constriction nerve injury pain model, and (iii) the analogues displayed various efficacies in reducing pain, and the most efficacious analogues were further investigated for their binding affinities at A3AR and
we have developed a new class of potent and orally bioavailable A3 adenosinergic agonists with high efficacy for the treatment of neuropathic and inflammatory pain.
we have identified a new series of potent, orally active A3 adenosinereceptor agonists for the treatment of chronic neuropathic pain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and biological evaluation of novel adenosine analogues with the potential to be developed as orally active drugs for the treatment of chronic pain.
the development of orally active A2A adenosine receptor agonists for treating chronic pain and other conditions.
the discovery, characterization, and development of novel A3AR agonistic compounds as potential therapeutics for the treatment of chronic neuropathic pain and other inflammatory diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a small N6-methylation is tolerated, and that a small N1-methyl group is required to maintain A3AR binding affinity, but not to maintain efficacy in vivo.
the 2-aryethynyl group is a key feature of A3 adenosinergic agonists for the treatment of chronic neuropathic pain.
the C2-aryethynyl group of A3AR agonism has been modified in a manner that has led to a significant increase in in vivo efficacy and duration.

we have identified a series of potent and orally bioavailable A3AR agonistic ligands that can be used for the treatment of chronic pain.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the C2-aryl-ethynyl group of N6-(3-cholrobenzyl)-C2-arylethenyl-2′-deoxyadenosine derivatives is a key structural feature for potent in vivo activity in neuropathic pain, with the pyrazine-2-yl group being optimal.
a simple modification of the C2-aryl moiety of A3AR agonistic N6-substituted 2-aryethynyl-adenosine derivatives can lead to a dramatic increase of the analgesic potency of the compounds.
a small N6-methanocarbanucleobase is sufficient for maintaining A3AR agonism in vivo.
